{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABYgXesw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhCEwl8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 21, "title": "Add legally redistributable one-click demo cartridges for MSX1 and MSX2", "body": "## Problem

The public browser emulator is already able to boot MSX1/MSX2 ROM cartridges and uses the appropriate bundled C-BIOS when a cartridge is loaded (#19). However, visitors must still supply a local `.rom`/`.bin` file or manually download one of our diagnostic cartridges and import it. Most first-time visitors do not own MSX ROMs and cannot easily try an actual playable game. We need a small, appealing **select a demo → play immediately** experience without distributing commercial/copyright-restricted ROMs.

Publicly available game downloads are **not** automatically licensed for redistribution. For every third-party demo ROM, binary redistribution rights and incorporated third-party assets must be checked and recorded independently of the emulator's MIT license.

## Expected outcome

The browser app offers a compact, discoverable **Demo ROMs** selector where a visitor can choose a legally redistributable game or demonstration and start it directly, without an external ROM, file picker, account, external website, emulator configuration, or third-party runtime network access.

Deliver an initial curated collection containing:
- **At least two worthwhile, playable third-party MSX1 cartridge games**, subject to confirmed ROM/binary redistribution rights and executable compatibility. Prioritized candidates from initial research are [PRJ_PLUS / plustaker](https://github.com/mazone-ma3/PRJ_PLUS) (MIT; 16 KiB `MSX1/BIN/plustakermsx.rom`) and [Westen House](https://github.com/santiontanon/westen) (Apache-2.0; official 48 KiB [v1.3.1 release ROM](https://github.com/santiontanon/westen/releases/tag/v1.3.1)). Investigate exact binary/asset licensing first; if either fails rights or emulator compatibility checks, replace it with a **verified** redistributable, working equivalent, not an unlicensed copy.
- **At least one MSX2-specific demo**, initially the project's already distributed, independently authored MIT-licensed **MSX2 diagnostic cartridge** (`msx2-test-cartridge.rom`, SCREEN 7/8). Additional third-party MSX2 games are welcome only if their binary and asset redistribution rights and machine compatibility are verified; do not make finding an unrelated MSX2 commercial-quality title a blocker.

Keep existing **Open ROM** for user-owned games and existing Weave BASIC starters. Include a short description, MSX model, controls and attribution/license link for each sample. The resulting site should let visitors explore real cartridge execution on both machines, not just screenshots or a simulated preview.

## Context and reproduction

- Repository `takahirox/msx-rust`; default branch `main`, at `cc80cc69fe62` when this Issue was drafted.
- Current architecture: independent Rust `msx-core`, `msx-wasm`, `web/app.js`, `web/index.html`, `scripts/build.sh`, `scripts/check-dist.mjs`, C-BIOS 0.29a. Issue #19 / PR #20 made both models boot Weave BASIC with no cartridge and switch to the matching C-BIOS when a cartridge is loaded under automatic firmware policy.
- Current `Open ROM` flow reads the local `File.arrayBuffer` and stages bytes with `msx_upload/msx_load`; it already supports plain ROMs, explicit mapper overrides, automatic inference with conservative failure, reset/eject and error state preservation. Reuse this loading path or its shared core operations, rather than duplicating emulation behavior.
- Previous candidate research also found [XSpelunker](https://github.com/santiontanon/xspelunker) (GPL-3.0, 32 KiB release ROM), which may be usable **only with all corresponding GPL binary/source obligations satisfied**, and [NEON REVENANT](https://github.com/kanon-ai/NEON_REVENANT) (MSX1/MSX2 512 KiB ROMs), whose project-specific license is explicitly **unspecified** and therefore **must not be bundled** without separate permission. Other freeware/MSXdev binaries likewise need per-title verification.
- The repository already provides self-authored original cartridge, C-BIOS service-test and MSX2 diagnostic ROMs with provenance. Keep them usable.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Provenance and redistribution rights

- [ ] Before bundling **each third-party game ROM**, verify an explicit license or direct permission that covers distribution of the **compiled ROM as a binary**, including packaged music, fonts, graphics and other assets. Check the exact release/version chosen, repo-specific notices and any upstream dependencies. **Do not infer redistributability solely from free downloads, open source visibility, tournament entry, or a source tree's license if ROM or assets are excluded.** Exclude unclear candidates; no owner approval or copyrighted-game input is required to continue with alternatives.
- [ ] Pin exact official source/release URLs, game title, creator, model, ROM size, mapper, version, and SHA-256 hashes in a tracked manifest. Keep each game under **its own verified upstream license** rather than relabeling it MIT; preserve copyright, attribution, license/NOTICE text and required source links or corresponding-source distributions. Record any changes from original binaries (prefer **unmodified** official ROM files).
- [ ] Prefer simple MIT/Apache-2.0 candidates. If including GPL-licensed compiled ROMs, separately satisfy all applicable license and corresponding-source availability obligations and document the compliance plan; do not inadvertently change the MIT licensing of unrelated original emulator code.
- [ ] Never bundle proprietary Microsoft/ASCII BIOS/BASIC, commercial games, unlicensed assets, or titles whose ROM redistribution rights are uncertain. Do not fetch third-party ROMs dynamically at runtime or proxy them via untrusted download services. All curated demo data must be verified static site assets available from the built deployment. Update the existing asset-provenance/legal documentation.

### Demo experience and firmware/mappers

- [ ] Add a concise discoverable Demo ROMs UI (e.g. within/below the existing screen controls or expandable advanced options) with the curated games and the MSX2 diagnostic. Each item exposes its machine, genre/purpose, controls, relevant mapper and license/author credit in a readable but uncluttered presentation, with a real **Play/Load demo** interaction.
- [ ] Starting a demo selects its **declared MSX1/MSX2 model** when needed and loads the bundled ROM through the existing Rust/Wasm cartridge API. In automatic firmware policy, use the matching bundled **C-BIOS** for cartridge launches, preserve the correct mapper explicitly if documented (do not force heuristic guessing for curated known ROMs), reset and start execution. No local ROM picker or network request outside the site's own static assets is required.
- [ ] Make demo switching, Reset, Eject and **Use Weave BASIC** predictable: switching demo replaces the active cartridge, Eject returns to Weave BASIC in the same model under automatic policy, Reset restarts the selected cartridge, and manually imported cartridges continue to work. Preserve the existing explicit local BIOS/firmware override semantics; demo loading must not silently overwrite a deliberate user-selected firmware mode.
- [ ] Handle async fetch/import failures, missing/tampered assets, unsupported mappings, and rapid repeated clicks safely. A failing demo load must **not** discard or corrupt the previously running BASIC program/cartridge or firmware/model selection; show a helpful error. Ensure fetches work under both root and the `/msx-rust/` Pages prefix with relative URLs. No ROM uploads, remote analytics, external execution or persistence.
- [ ] Do not present a file imported into memory as proof a game is playable. Include only cartridges that demonstrably boot and offer meaningful visible interaction in this emulator, and document unsupported features/limitations. Third-party MSX1 games should be tested under MSX1; optionally verify MSX2 backward compatibility separately.

### Reproducible tests, docs, deployment

- [ ] Add automated checks for the pinned demo manifest and **exact file hashes/sizes**, licensing notices and source attribution, and ensure every included ROM is accounted for in `./scripts/build.sh`, `scripts/check-dist.mjs` and the deployed Pages artifact. Builds/tests must be reproducible without downloading third-party files at test time.
- [ ] Add Playwright end-to-end tests that choose each included ROM directly from the new Demo ROMs UI in the compiled Wasm app and verify **observable emulated execution** (Canvas pixels or VRAM-based output and at least one meaningful keyboard/joystick input response for game ROMs), proper model/mapper/firmware state, Reset/Eject, switching demo, and safe recovery from missing/static-asset fetch failures. Run at both `/` and `/msx-rust/`. No proprietary ROMs or human game testing are required.
- [ ] Preserve previous MSX1/MSX2 Weave BASIC, original diagnostic, C-BIOS service-test, mapper inference/override, file picker, browser focus/audio, full-screen and responsive mobile workflows. Document how to select/play demos and where to find each copyright/license/source, without implying that all online/free MSX ROMs may be redistributed.
- [ ] Run and report `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, and `npm test`, with browser screenshot evidence as appropriate. Follow the repository's English Issue → implementation → PR → AI review → merge flow. Subjective owner play-testing or a physical MSX is **not** a pre-merge gate.

## Optional validation

- After merge the owner may play the curated games using keyboard or controller and report gameplay/audio/compatibility issues as **separate follow-up Issues**. Additional licensed MSX2 games, new genres, thumbnails and a larger gallery are future work, not conditions for this initial complete ROM-free visitor demo experience.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] After merge, verify the **live** https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/ deployment and record its Actions run and commit. On the real published site, select at least one independently licensed third-party MSX1 game and the original MSX2 diagnostic from Demo ROMs, observe running video and a working input/control path, verify Reset/Eject/BASIC restoration, and verify all bundled ROMs/licenses load at their deployed URLs with no errors. This is **after merge**, not a PR approval gate; file separate follow-up Issues for live-site defects.
